tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own product page states the device has its own LED screen that displays the SpO2 and pulse-rate reading directly, and that the free iHealth MyVitals app (backed by iHealth Cloud) is something you 'can' pair for extra history and waveform visualization, not something setup requires. Core function (taking and displaying a reading) works with the device never paired to anything, and the vendor's cloud is a named, optional add-on, which is the D2 row on the decision table.
the_unplug_test: Turn it on, clip it to a finger, and the number appears on the device's own LED screen within seconds — no phone required at all. What the Bluetooth link and the MyVitals app add is a continuous history, a plethysmograph waveform, and a perfusion index; without them you still get the same SpO2 and pulse-rate reading the device exists to produce, you just do not get a log of past readings, since the device does not appear to keep one on its own.
offline_losses: trend history and logging of past readings over time
in-app plethysmograph waveform and perfusion-index visualization
iHealth Cloud sync and any sharing features tied to the MyVitals app

repairability.notes: Sealed body with a built-in rechargeable 3.7V/390mAh Li-ion battery charged over USB rather than user-replaceable; no teardown checked.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: model PO3, 'large digital LED screen' displays results on the device itself, Bluetooth 4.0 BLE, and the free iHealth MyVitals app is described as something the device 'can' be paired with for extra tracking, waveform and perfusion-index visualization rather than as a requirement. Confirms specs (SpO2 70-99% +/-2%, pulse 30-250bpm, rechargeable battery, ~300 uses/charge) and current price $39.99 (list $42.99).

FCC ID search for grantee iHealth Labs, Inc. (grantee code SLR, Sunnyvale CA) lists roughly 100 grants, nearly all Bluetooth-connected health devices (blood pressure monitors, scales, glucose meters, thermometers, activity trackers) paired to the same iHealth MyVitals app/iHealth Cloud ecosystem. No FCC grant specifically for the PO3/Air pulse oximeter was located in the search results, which may reflect an incomplete result set rather than a genuine absence — not used to support a radio-absence claim here, only to corroborate that iHealth's standard pattern across its product line is BLE-to-optional-cloud-app.

open_questions: Whether the iHealth MyVitals app itself requires creating an iHealth account to open and pair with the device, or only to enable cloud sync, was not directly confirmed — app-store listings could not be fetched. Recorded as account_required: app_only on the assumption the account gate, if any, sits behind the optional app rather than the device.
Could not locate an FCC grant specifically for the PO3/Air model despite searching the iHealth Labs grantee list; fcc_id left null rather than guessed.
Whether the device itself retains any onboard memory of past readings (as opposed to the app storing history) was not confirmed by the spec sheet.

No FDA 510(k) clearance for this model was found in openFDA under iHealth Labs — unclear whether it is sold as a regulated medical device or as a consumer/wellness product; worth confirming before citing it for clinical use.
Firmware update / forced-OTA behavior over Bluetooth not established.
notes: A direct, cheaper counterpart to the pattern already established by omron-bp5255 in this category: a vendor cloud and app exist and add real value (trend history, waveform detail) but the base measurement the device exists to produce is not gated behind either. Good candidate for a second pulse-oximeter record from a different vendor (e.g. a Contec/Wellue BLE model) to compare against, but that research did not complete within budget on this run — Contec's own domain (contecmed.com) returned TLS certificate errors on every fetch attempt.
local_replacement_note: No self-hosted or third-party replacement for iHealth Cloud/MyVitals was found. The device's own LED display is the only local output; there is no on-device history to fall back on beyond the current reading.
